us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic developments from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Trump administration says it will remove 760,000 ACA enrollees over fraud claims
bullets: Vice President JD Vance said officials found fraudulent or nonexistent marketplace enrollments.
The administration projected $2.2 billion in savings from canceled subsidy payments.
Officials also announced a six-month suspension on new brokers enrolling people in coverage.

articles.title: New York and California sue over federal offshore wind lease buybacks
bullets: The states are challenging Trump administration deals to cancel offshore wind projects.
The disputed deals would pay energy companies $1.4 billion to walk away from projects.
Attorneys general said the cancellations could raise electricity costs and hinder clean-energy goals.

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue over Trump White House press ban
bullets: The outlets sued after being barred from White House access over the weekend.
Their lawsuit argues the ban violates First Amendment press protections.
Other media organizations condemned the restrictions and raised due-process concerns.

articles.title: Trump signs US-Denmark-Greenland Arctic security agreement
bullets: The agreement is aimed at strengthening Arctic and North Atlantic security cooperation.
It follows months of tension over Trump’s calls for Greenland to become part of the United States.
Greenland’s prime minister called the accord a “win-win-win agreement,” according to AP’s live coverage.

articles.title: Trump and Xi seek stability as AI, trade and Iran tensions flare
bullets: Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting Washington for talks with President Donald Trump.
The leaders are expected to discuss AI competition, trade commitments, Iran and Taiwan.
Officials signaled no grand bargain is expected, but both sides are trying to steady relations.

global.label: Global
global.subtitle: Major world stories and conflicts in focus

articles.title: US and Iran hold mediated UN talks after Trump’s ‘annihilation’ warning
bullets: US and Iranian officials held contacts on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Qatar and other mediators were involved in efforts to de-escalate the war.
Iranian officials described the UN gathering as an opportunity to return to negotiations.

articles.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with drones before Zelenskyy’s UN address
bullets: Russian daylight drone attacks hit Kyiv on Wednesday.
Officials reported two people killed and 23 wounded in the capital.
The strikes came hours before President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was due to address the UN General Assembly.

articles.title: Gaza students return to in-person schooling for first time in three years
bullets: Hundreds of thousands of children returned to classes in Gaza.
Many schools are damaged or operating from makeshift buildings and tents.
Families still face high costs for basic supplies such as uniforms, notebooks and pens.

articles.title: Catholic clergy march to Vatican demanding end to Gaza ‘genocide’
bullets: About 150 priests, friars, a bishop and nuns marched toward the Vatican.
The group prayed in front of St. Peter’s Square and carried names of children killed in Gaza and Lebanon.
The turnout was larger than a similar march the group held last year.

articles.title: UN General Assembly opens amid wars in Iran, Gaza, Ukraine, Sudan and Myanmar
bullets: World leaders gathered in New York for the annual high-level UN meeting.
The agenda is dominated by major conflicts, climate change, inequality and economic turmoil.
Diplomats are also confronting questions about the UN’s future and effectiveness.

india.label: India News
india.subtitle: Top India developments from politics, economy, weather and science

articles.title: Supreme Court says people cannot be penalised for not singing Vande Mataram
bullets: The court addressed the issue during proceedings involving Carnatic singer T M Krishna.
It said refusal to sing the national song cannot carry penal consequences.
The case has drawn wider debate over patriotic expression and compelled speech.

articles.title: Election Commissioners reportedly objected 14 times to poll-panel moves
bullets: The Indian Express reported objections by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
The objections concerned voter forms, roll changes and centralisation of voter-software systems.
Opposition parties cited the report to question Election Commission independence.

articles.title: Deep depression nears Andhra-Odisha coast, prompting school closures and alerts
bullets: Odisha placed 11 districts on high alert as the system approached the coast.
Schools, Anganwadi centres and tourist sites were ordered shut in affected areas.
Authorities warned of heavy rain and rough conditions as the system moved inland.

articles.title: Two J&K policemen found dead inside car in Ramban
bullets: The two officers were found unconscious in a car Tuesday night in Sanasar, Ramban district.
They were taken to Ramban district hospital and declared brought dead.
Police registered a case and took three people for questioning.

articles.title: ISRO and ESA renew space cooperation agreement through 2032
bullets: ISRO and the European Space Agency extended their long-standing cooperation pact.
The agreement was signed at the International Space Summit in Paris.
New focus areas include space weather, robotic exploration and space sustainability.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Market movers and trading themes affecting US-listed shares

articles.title: Meta shares draw bullish calls as Muse AI gains traction
bullets: Reuters reported Wall Street analysts turned more bullish on Meta’s AI agent Muse.
JPMorgan said Muse could become one of the most widely used consumer AI apps since ChatGPT.
Meta’s rally added momentum to the broader AI trade in US equities.

articles.title: On Holding jumps after unveiling new financial goals
bullets: US-listed shares of On Holding rose sharply in Tuesday trading.
The Swiss sportswear company presented updated financial targets to investors.
The move stood out on an otherwise quieter day for Wall Street.

articles.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery rise on merger-settlement reports
bullets: Reuters reported both stocks jumped after settlement talks advanced with California officials.
The settlement clears a major hurdle for Paramount’s proposed Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition.
The deal would help Paramount avoid a $7 million daily fee after September 30.

articles.title: Nasdaq hits record close as AI optimism offsets oil worries
bullets: The tech-heavy Nasdaq set a record closing high on Tuesday.
Reuters cited continued strength in AI-linked technology shares.
Oil prices and Treasury yields dipped as crude flows through the Middle East improved.

articles.title: Wall Street holds near record as Brent briefly slips below $98
bullets: US stocks hovered near record territory as crude prices eased.
Lower oil prices reduced pressure on inflation-sensitive and fuel-sensitive sectors.
Investors also watched bond yields and Middle East peace signals.

articles.title: States settle lawsuit over Paramount-Warner merger, clearing key hurdle
bullets: Twelve states and Hollywood writers had challenged Paramount’s buyout of Warner Bros.
The settlement includes commitments on US film production and worker support funds.
Paramount CEO David Ellison said the agreement marked complete clearance for the merger.

articles.title: GM CEO Mary Barra expected at Trump’s state dinner for Xi
bullets: Reuters reported Barra is expected to attend Thursday’s White House state dinner.
US automakers have warned against allowing Chinese manufacturers into the US market.
Other executives from Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla are also expected to attend.

articles.title: Apple pitches new Macs as lower-cost alternative to AI data-center rentals
bullets: Apple’s upgraded Mac Minis and Mac Studios are aimed at corporate AI workloads.
The company is pitching local AI processing to reduce dependence on cloud tokens.
The machines will compete with Nvidia-linked PCs and Microsoft’s coming Windows AI hardware push.

articles.title: India business activity rebounds to three-month high in September
bullets: HSBC’s flash India Composite PMI rose to 56.5 from 54.3 in August.
Manufacturing and services both expanded faster as domestic demand improved.
Export momentum and services hiring were weaker, tempering the broader outlook.

articles.title: Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub foundation planned for October 2
bullets: N Chandrababu Naidu and Nirmala Sitharaman are set to lay the foundation at Madanapalle.
The project proposes ₹40,000 crore in central support and ₹60,000 crore in private investment.
It is expected to cover six districts in Andhra Pradesh’s Rayalaseema region.

tech.label: Tech
tech.subtitle: AI, chips and platform news driving the technology sector

articles.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna
bullets: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Sol and Luna for the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work.
The company said the models bring GPT-6 Astra advances into faster, cheaper tiers.
OpenAI listed API prices at $2 per million input tokens for Sol and $0.10 for Luna.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5
bullets: Anthropic said Opus 5.5 is the first model in its Claude 5.5 family.
The company said it performs at Fable 5.1 level on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5.
Anthropic said external evaluators tested the model before release.

articles.title: Alibaba unveils new powerful AI chip and model plans
bullets: Alibaba announced a new AI chip as Chinese firms push deeper into advanced computing.
The move comes amid intensifying US-China competition over AI hardware and models.
AP noted US AI leaders have warned about China’s AI-development pace.

articles.title: US proposes AI incident alert system in talks with China
bullets: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US proposed a notification mechanism for AI incidents.
The idea was raised ahead of Trump-Xi talks at the White House.
Officials framed the system as a way to manage national-security risks from AI.

articles.title: Meta’s Muse AI app outpaces ChatGPT’s early mobile launch
bullets: TechCrunch reported Meta’s Muse is showing strong early app-download momentum.
Muse is positioned as a personal AI agent for everyday digital tasks.
Its rise has strengthened investor focus on Meta’s consumer AI strategy ahead of Meta Connect.
